meta.description: Registry for equivalence-related failure modes in Phase 2 of the Mono-Process Formal Law Program.

failure_modes.name: false_equivalence
failure_modes.description: Two formally distinct objects are incorrectly classified as equivalent.

failure_modes.name: over_collapse
failure_modes.description: Equivalence class merge results in the loss of critical process information required for closure.

failure_modes.name: under_collapse
failure_modes.description: Failure to merge equivalent states leads to branch explosion or non-convergence.

failure_modes.name: context_drift
failure_modes.description: Equivalence relationship fails when the surrounding residue, orientation, or admissibility context changes.

failure_modes.name: non_transitive_equivalence
failure_modes.description: Relationships A~B and B~C do not imply A~C, violating formal equivalence requirements.

failure_modes.name: orientation_aliasing
failure_modes.description: Distinct orientation frames are treated as equivalent, leading to selection conflicts.

failure_modes.name: residue_aliasing
failure_modes.description: Distinct residue histories are treated as equivalent, leading to incorrect admissibility conditioning.

failure_modes.name: admissibility_aliasing
failure_modes.description: Non-admissible states are incorrectly classed with admissible states.

failure_modes.name: projection_aliasing
failure_modes.description: Forward projection erases critical distinctions required for unique preimage recovery.

failure_modes.name: branch_collapse_error
failure_modes.description: Merging non-equivalent branches results in formal derivation leakage or instability.

failure_modes.name: reconstruction_class_ambiguity
failure_modes.description: Reconstruction results in multiple distinct equivalence classes rather than a unique one.
